background: Coventry Building Society is the second-largest UK building society after Nationwide, a mutual funded by retail savings and lending almost entirely on residential and buy-to-let mortgages, and the owner of The Co-operative Bank.
synthesis: Rated A- on average across two of the three, both on a stable outlook, the society was downgraded one notch by one of the three on 16 Sep 2026, with the cut tied to a narrowing buffer of capital protecting senior debt. CET1 of 19.6% is in the top quarter of UK building societies, but leverage of 4.8% is in the bottom quarter, which is the weak spot. Liquidity is strong, with LCR of 232% and NSFR of 147% both above their medians. The trend is downward: since 30 Jun 2025 CET1 has fallen 1.6 points, leverage 0.5 points and LCR 19 points, while NSFR has been broadly flat.
